notes:
Businesses your site lists are no longer reported as your own premises.

If a page publishes structured data about other companies — a directory, a
marketplace, a "restaurants near you" listing — those entries sit inside an
ItemList. Docket read the first of them as if it described the audited business
itself, and reported that the site was missing its own address, telephone,
opening hours, map location and price range. On a national food-delivery site
every one of those facts belonged to a takeaway the site lists.

Docket now judges the site's own markup whenever it has any. Where the only
local markup describes businesses the site lists, the finding says so, names the
business it is about, and states plainly that it is not a claim about the site's
own address or opening hours. It is reported as a lower-priority listing-quality
issue, because that is what it is: complete listing entries are what make a
directory page eligible for rich results.

The sentence explaining why the local checks ran was corrected in the same way,
and no longer tells a marketplace it looks like a restaurant.
